text.arabic_uthmani: كَلَّآ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ دَكًّۭا دَكًّۭا

words.gloss_range: emphatic rebuke and refusal that arrests the preceding moral frame before opening the eschatological scene
words.prose: {{ar:كَلَّآ}} ({{tr:kallā}}) is not a neutral scene-opener. It first blocks the preceding logic of security, wealth, and desire, then lets the coming earth-collapse answer that logic. Because the particle stands outside the when-clause and carries no root imagery, its force comes from discourse position: refusal before explanation, rebuke before the threshold. Even its held opening sound helps the ayah pause at refusal before the next temporal scene begins.

topics.headline: rebuke before the eschatological threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by rejecting the preceding moral logic before showing the catastrophic answer.
topics.reason: The QAC row identifies an emphatic response and rebuke particle, and attachment support marks the preceding context window as relevant before the temporal clause begins.

topics.headline: particle outside the when-clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the refusal is not simply a complement inside the when-clause but a discourse halt before that clause.
topics.reason: The temporal clause is marked as beginning at word 2, leaving word 1 as a prior discourse particle.

topics.headline: fixed particle carries the turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a compact function word, not a lexical root image, performs the opening reversal.
topics.reason: The aligned word is tagged as a particle with no root, while its grammar carries rebuke and reversal.

topics.headline: returning refusal and held sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the refusal as a boundary sound that carries the social indictment into the collapse scene.
topics.reason: The row family links the particle to the preceding indictment and to the immediate transition into the temporal threshold.

words.gloss_range: eventive when-threshold that opens a future conditional scene and holds its consequence beyond the local ayah
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) turns the collapse into a threshold rather than a freestanding report. It points forward to the moment when the earth is crushed, while the perfect passive inside its clause makes that future event feel already sealed. Because the particle itself is fixed and uninflected, its force is read from position: a light temporal entry is immediately compressed by the heavy crushing verb. The syntax also withholds full closure: the listener must carry this when-clause into the following arrival and judgment scene, so 89:21 functions as the opening condition of a larger sequence.

topics.headline: future threshold with completed force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coming collapse is introduced as future and yet already completed in aspect.
topics.reason: The particle opens an eventive temporal frame, and the governed verb is a perfect passive.

topics.headline: when-clause held open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels 89:21 as an unfinished condition whose answer accumulates in the next scene.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks word 2 as opening the temporal scene; the CRITICAL rows correctly press the delayed scope of that scene.

topics.headline: decisive eventive threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reads the word as the trigger-point of collapse, not as a vague stretch of time.
topics.reason: The QAC and attachment rows both treat the particle as governing an eventive temporal clause.

topics.headline: light entry into impact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the uninflected particle gains force from position and from its immediate movement into the heavy crushing verb.
topics.reason: The particle has no inflectional marking, so its force is carried by placement before the passive clause.

topics.headline: threshold anticipates 89:22
topics.reader_payoff: The reader carries the crushing forward into the next ayah, where the event frame continues (89:22).
topics.reason: The rows name the forward dependency, and the local clause evidence supports a temporal frame rather than an isolated assertion.

words.gloss_range: passive perfect crushing and leveling of the earth, with the agent unexpressed and the following cognate accusatives carrying repeated intensity
words.root_gloss_range: root range centered here on crushing, demolishing, pounding, compacting, and leveling; other dictionary branches such as soil-covering, crowding, or platform senses are not locally selected
words.prose: {{ar:دُكَّتِ}} ({{tr:dukkati}}) is the clause's engine: a passive perfect that makes the earth bear the collapse while leaving the crusher unnamed. Its feminine ending already locks the impact to the earth before the noun's full scale is unfolded. The local root pressure is physical reduction, not gentle smoothing or abstract defeat; stable ground is broken toward levelness. The verb itself is not an iterative stem, so the ayah separates patient-focused received action from repetition, which the two following cognate accusatives supply. Its rare d-k-k field and the earth-and-mountains crushing scene (69:14) make the local scene feel formally marked, while 89:22 follows only after the ground has been leveled.

topics.headline: passive patient-focus with unexpressed agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the collapse from the side of the earth being acted upon, while the agent is left unexpressed.
topics.reason: The aligned verb is passive, has no expressed object or agent, and governs the event whose subject is the earth.

topics.headline: agreement locks the verb to earth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the feminine ending ties the impact to the earth before the noun is even fully processed.
topics.reason: The subject attachment and QAC grammar identify feminine agreement with the following earth noun.

topics.headline: crushing toward leveled aftermath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the verb as forceful terrain-reduction, not as a bland change of state.
topics.reason: V4 accepts the crushing and leveling branch, and the local subject is the earth.

topics.headline: received action, repetition supplied later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the finite verb presents received crushing, while repeated impact is pushed into the later doublet.
topics.reason: The local finite form is passive Form I; the following two gerunds carry the repetition by cognate accusative construction.

topics.headline: rare d-k-k earth-crushing field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader links this verb to a rare Quranic earth-crushing field, including the earth-and-mountains crushing scene (69:14).
topics.reason: Contextual profiles mark the passive d-k-k form as low occurrence and include 69:14 among the same-form implicit-agent references.

topics.headline: verb echoed by doublet and boundary reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verb answered by its own root echo as the previous excess gives way to leveling.
topics.reason: The attachments identify the two following same-root cognate accusatives, and the CRITICAL boundary rows tie that echo to the discourse turn.

topics.headline: collapse before arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 89:22 arrives only after the passive collapse has already framed the ground.
topics.reason: The row's concrete 89:22 contrast is consistent with the temporal sequence opened by word 2.

words.gloss_range: the definite earth or ground-domain as known support, passive subject, and inhabited substrate being crushed
words.root_gloss_range: earth, land, ground, soil, territory, and inhabited realm; local grammar concentrates that range into the definite support-domain under collapse
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضُ}} ({{tr:al-arḍu}}) is not the object of an active seizure; it is the nominative passive subject that bears the collapse. Its definiteness gathers the familiar support-domain beneath human life, not an indefinite patch of soil, and compresses soil, land, terrain, and inhabited world into one threatened domain. The common earth noun is locally constrained by the rare d-k-k environment: crushing appears before it and the repeated manner follows it, placing the ground at the hinge of the ayah's impact. Inter-ayah contrasts sharpen the choice: 99:1 shakes the earth, 84:3 stretches it, 14:48 replaces it, and earth and mountains are crushed together (69:14), while 89:21 makes reduction of the ground itself the defining event. The boundary also shifts from what humans love and possess to the ground that makes possession possible.

topics.headline: earth as passive subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the earth grammatically bears the passive collapse rather than appearing as an active verb's object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the noun the passive subject of the preceding verb, and the QAC row marks it nominative.

topics.headline: known ground as inhabited support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the collapse as an attack on the shared ground and support-system beneath habitation.
topics.reason: The noun is definite and concrete; V4 lacks root rows for this root, so local grammar and CRITICAL evidence preserve the support-domain payoff.

topics.headline: earth range compressed into one domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that soil, land, terrain, and inhabited world are compressed into one definite earth-domain.
topics.reason: The definite singular concrete noun supports a totalizing local range without requiring plural land-forms.

topics.headline: earth enclosed by d-k-k forms
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the earth positioned between the crushing verb and the repeated crushing nouns, as if syntactically enclosed by impact.
topics.reason: The noun is attached as subject between the passive d-k-k verb and two same-root cognate accusatives.

topics.headline: crushing among earth transformation scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes this earth-scene from shaking (99:1), stretching (84:3), replacement (14:48), and the earth-and-mountains crushing pattern (69:14).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete references, and the contextual evidence supports the earth noun as a common creation-domain term locally constrained by d-k-k.

topics.headline: from possession to ground
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the discourse shift from what humans possess to the ground that makes possession possible.
topics.reason: The local noun is concrete earth without an explicit heaven-earth pair, and the boundary rows link it to the preceding value-field.

words.gloss_range: first accusative cognate verbal noun naming the manner and intensity of the passive crushing and opening the repeated doublet
words.root_gloss_range: root range centered here on crushing, pounding, compacting, pulverizing, and leveling; the local gerund makes the process explicit as a cognate accusative
words.prose: The first {{ar:دَكًّۭا}} ({{tr:dakkan}}) turns the verb's event into an explicit process: crushing as the manner and measure of what happens to the earth. Its accusative verbal-noun form keeps it attached to the passive verb, so the unnamed agent does not weaken intensity. In that passive scene it can carry received-collapse coloring, while the local form remains a gerund naming applied force rather than a different reflexive verb. As the first half of an exact doublet, the word is open to immediate repetition; no conjunction interrupts the sequence, and the compact, rare sound prepares the second blow. Its intensified cadence also answers the immediately preceding moral excess with intensified leveling.

topics.headline: first cognate accusative specifies manner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that crushing is grammatically restated as the event's own measure, not merely inferred from the verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks word 5 as a same-root cognate accusative attached to the passive verb.

topics.headline: crushing process made explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels a concrete process of pounding, compaction, and reduction rather than a softened leveling.
topics.reason: The accepted V4 branch centers on crushing and demolishing until leveled, matching the local same-root gerund.

topics.headline: received-collapse coloring under passive context
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first gerund as applied force in a passive scene, with received-collapse coloring but not a different local form.
topics.reason: The local word is a gerund, not a reflexive finite form; the passive context can color the process without replacing the local morphology.

topics.headline: first half of the exact doublet
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first unit as prepared for exact repetition, so one manner noun becomes the start of a process.
topics.reason: The second same-root gerund is attached as a repeated cognate accusative, making the first word the opening unit of a doublet.

topics.headline: compact first blow answers excess
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a compact first blow whose intensity answers the immediately preceding moral excess.
topics.reason: The gerund is low occurrence, part of a marked passive-plus-repeated-cognate construction, and the boundary row ties the intensified form to the prior discourse.

words.gloss_range: second matching accusative verbal noun that intensifies the first into repeated, distributive, and total crushing
words.root_gloss_range: root range centered here on repeated crushing, pounding, compacting, and leveling; exact lexical doubling supplies iteration without changing the local form
words.prose: The second {{ar:دَكًّۭا}} ({{tr:dakkan}}) does not add a new object or a new clause; it repeats the first accusative measure and makes recurrence itself the form of intensity. Because it is bare, appositive, and unjoined, the final cadence feels compressed rather than listed. Exact duplication turns crushing into succession, distribution, and completeness, while the hard repeated d-k-k sound closes the ayah with the impact it names. The repeated rare gerund keeps the same earth-crushing field active through the ayah's last word. The doublet also prepares the doubled ranks of the following scene (89:22), linking collapse to arranged arrival, and it turns prior accumulation and excess into exhaustive leveling.

topics.headline: second accusative intensifies the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second word as intensifying the same manner-force, not introducing a separate argument.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second gerund as a same-root cognate accusative that repeats the first.

topics.headline: exact repetition creates totalizing force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same crushing force spread across the whole surface through exact repetition.
topics.reason: The local form duplicates the first gerund exactly, and the accepted V4 branch supports crushing and leveling as the active field.

topics.headline: iteration by lexical doubling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that repeated pounding is achieved by exact word repetition rather than by shifting to a different derived stem.
topics.reason: The local second word is the same gerund form as word 5; no alternate iterative surface is present.

topics.headline: unjoined percussive close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah close with compressed repeated impact rather than a coordinated list.
topics.reason: The two gerunds stand adjacent without a conjunction, and both are marked as repeated cognate accusatives.

topics.headline: doublet prepares 89:22
topics.reader_payoff: The reader carries the doubled crushing cadence into the doubled ranks of the next scene (89:22).
topics.reason: The concrete forward reference is coherent with the temporal sequence opened in 89:21 and continued in 89:22.

topics.headline: excess answered by exhaustive leveling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees prior accumulation and excess answered by a double image of reduction.
topics.reason: The boundary rows tie the final doublet to the preceding moral charge, and the context-window evidence supports reading the transition across ayahs.

topics.headline: rare gerund repeated immediately
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that an uncommon d-k-k gerund becomes the ayah's final two-word formal density.
topics.reason: Contextual profiles mark the gerund as low occurrence and strongly tied to the same-root passive construction.

strongest_changes: The monumental sequence makes the focus an exact reversal of supporting, shaping, cutting, and anchoring durable height.
Partition, enclosure, bounded land, inheritance, and property turn flat earth into cadastral erasure as well as geology.
Gathered and overfull wealth before the focus becomes straight repeated rows after it, so levelling functions as a heap-to-array transform.
The social sequence converts crowding and heavy tread into a load borne by unsupported people at the lowest ground.
The later composed soul distinguishes violent imposed lowing from inward stable settling.
summary.what_was_special: The same two focus roots sustained destructive, hydraulic, architectural, legal, social, procedural, bodily, temporal, and ecological readings without forcing them into one interpretation. Most distinctive were the formal transform from accumulated heap to ordered rows, the erasure of property-bearing boundaries, and the split-root mortar and tremor activations.
remaining_uncertainties: The hydraulic, cadastral, social-load, and heap-to-array arrows are abductive connections supplied by the reader rather than explicit causal statements in the packet.
The complete-span focus branch and the non-dominant time, mortar, and speech-tremor branches are valid packet material but remain form-distant.
The seedbed and path-preparation readings preserve material continuity but must not displace the focus's strongly destructive baseline.
The platform reading may denote a result of levelling or may be only a lexical echo sharpened by the following rows.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The ground that held power is leveled.** Lexical evidence: `د ك ك B001` crushing/demolishing until leveled; `د ك ك B002` flat low spread-outness; `ء ر ض B001` lower ground opposite sky. Structural cue: repeated `دكًّا دكًّا` echoes the earlier repetitions of claims and intensifiers while reversing pillars, rock, and pegs. Assigned role: the earth becomes the surface on which every vertical or fixed power is flattened. Abductive move: I infer that earlier built images are the implied targets of leveling; the packet supplies pillars, rocks, pegs, and earth-crushing. Reading change: the ayah reads as material deconstruction of the previous civilizational grammar.

2. **Burial-covering and crowd-pressure.** Lexical evidence: `د ك ك B003` covering/filling with soil over a dead person; `د ك ك B008` crowding and pressing together; `ء ر ض B006` sticking to ground and lingering. Structural cue: after accumulated eating/loving, the whole earth is pressed repeatedly. Assigned role: the repeated crushing compresses social excess into a final ground-level condition. Abductive move: I infer that the earth-event is both demolition and burial-pressure, because later 89:22-23 bring ordered rows and remembrance after compression. Reading change: the ayah becomes a transition from inflated appetite to pressed exposure.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 89:22’s rows made `د ك ك B008` visible: the earth is pressed and cleared so a new ordered arrangement can appear.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Material leveling as reversal of social elevation.** **Evidence/cue:** `د ك ك B001/B002` supplies crushing until level and flat low spread-outness; `ء ر ض B001` is the lower ground opposite the sky. The backward half-window contrasts measured scarcity with honor-claims, withheld care, consolidated inheritance, and abundant wealth, while 89:22 places lordly arrival and ordered rows above the leveled field. **Mechanism:** crushing removes the vertical differences on which claims to elevated worth and possession rested. The packet supplies social asymmetry, leveling, and a new order; I infer the corrective relation. **Reading change:** the repeated *dakkan* is not generic destruction but a physical abolition of manufactured hierarchy.

2. **Private aggregation turned into universal compression.** **Evidence/cue:** `د ك ك B008` is crowding and pressing together, recalling total gathering through `ل م م B001` in 89:19; 89:22 then arranges rows through `ص ف ف B001`, and 89:25-26 twice isolates “anyone” through `ء ح د B002`. **Mechanism:** what people privately gathered is answered by the gathering of people themselves, first compressed and then ordered for individual encounter. The packet supplies all three spatial operations; their sequence is inferred as reversal. **Reading change:** the reduplication makes leveling a social re-sorting process as well as a geological event.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 89:22 converted flatness into a prepared surface for rows, so leveling became reordering rather than mere ruin. 89:25-26 then supplied repeated *ahad*, correcting the crowding branch `د ك ك B008`: compression gathers everyone, but does not erase individual encounter.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yumuşak, iyi ve verimli toprağı merkez alır; bitkinin köklenip çoğalması veya biçilecek duruma gelmesi ile oğlağın bu ottan yiyip semirmesi buna bağlı gelişmelerdir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Toprağın niteliği çekirdektir; bitkinin gelişmesi ve oğlağın beslenmesi sonuç ya da ilişkili kullanım olarak kalmalıdır.

concept_map.definition: Belirtilen yapılarda yumuşak, iyi, verimli ve bol bitki yetiştiren toprağı anlatır. Buna bağlı yapılarda bitkinin toprağa iyice yerleşip çoğalması veya biçilebilir olması, köklü fidan ve yer bitkisini yiyen oğlak; ayrı bir kaynak kullanımında ise semiz oğlak ifade edilir.

facets.statement: Toprak veya çayırlık yumuşak, verimli ve iyi bitki yetiştirir.

Oğlak yer bitkisini yer.
Bir kaynakta ilgili niteleme semiz oğlağı belirtir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Tek kaynak ifadesi, sabit bir adlandırmanın doğrudan yabancı kimse anlamına geldiğini belirtir; yer sakini veya soy bağına ilişkin daha ayrıntılı bir koşul kurmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız kanıtlanan sabit söz birimine bağlanır; parçaların yalın anlamlarından yeni bir kişi sınıfı türetilmez.

facets.statement: Sabit söz birimi, bir yerde yabancı olan kimseyi adlandırır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin bulunduğu yere veya topluluğa ait olmaması anlamını korur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün aday kartlar değerlendirildi; genel yabancı anlamına en yakın, fakat topluluk koşuluyla ayrılan komşu seçildi.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın adın kanıtlanan nesne anlamıyla sınırlıdır ve komşu döşeme türlerinin özelliklerini içeri almaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Sağlanan kartların tümü değerlendirildi; nesne türü bakımından en yakın fakat kapsamı daha geniş döşeme komşusu yayımlandı.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişinin yere bağlı kalmasını, yere doğru ağırlaşmasını ve bunun sonucu oyalanıp gecikmesini aynı hareket durumu içinde verir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın eylem dalının yere bağlı kalma, ağırlaşma ve gecikme bileşenleriyle sınırlıdır.

facets.statement: Kişi yerden ayrılmayarak yere bağlı kalır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yere bağlılık, ağırlaşma ve gecikme bileşenlerini tek bir eylem karşılığında toplar.

error_profile.preserves: Yere yönelişi, ağırlığı, yerinde kalmayı ve bunun doğurduğu oyalanmayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin doğrudan yere bağlı kalması öne çıktığında kullanılabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da yere yakın durma ve bulunulan yerden ayrılmama durumu vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kişinin yere doğru ağırlaşıp gecikmesini anlatır; komşu dal farklı canlı ve nesnelerde yere yapışma ya da sabit kalma alanına daha geniş yayılır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; yere bağlı kalma çekirdeğini en doğrudan paylaşan ve kapsam farkını gösteren komşu seçildi.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kişiler arası karşıya çıkışı öne çıkarır; komşu dal bakma, gözetme ve genel yüzünü dönme kullanımlarını da kapsar.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Tüm komşular değerlendirildi; yönelme ve karşıya çıkma çekirdeğini en yakından paylaşan aday yayımlandı.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın hastalık çekirdeğini Türkçede en doğal ve ayırt edici biçimde karşılar.

facets.statement: Kişinin akıl ve beden durumu görünmez varlıkların etkisine bağlanır.
Etkilenen kişi başını ve gövdesini bilinçli bir amaç olmadan hareket ettirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek kanıt, doğaüstü varlıklara bağlanan akıl karışıklığını ve istemsiz baş-gövde hareketini aynı kişi durumunun ayrılmaz parçaları olarak verir.

concept_gloss.text: doğaüstü etkiye bağlanan istemsiz sarsıntılı akıl bozukluğu
concept_gloss.applicability: Neden yorumunu, akıl durumunu ve belirleyici istemsiz beden hareketini birlikte açıklar.

error_profile.preserves: Görünmez varlık etkisi yorumunu, akıl bozukluğunu ve istemsiz baş-gövde hareketini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin gözlenebilir beden hareketi ön plana çıkarıldığında açıklayıcı karşılık olarak kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Baş ve gövdenin bilinçli amaç olmadan hareket etmesi belirtisini korur.
error_profile.loses: Akıl bozukluğunu ve durumun görünmez varlıkların etkisine bağlanmasını dışarıda bırakır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: görünmez varlıkların etkisine bağlanan, başını ve gövdesini istemsizce hareket ettiren kişi

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yerle ilişkilendirilen görünmez varlıklar açıklamasını ve istemsiz baş-gövde hareketini birlikte taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Doğaüstü bir dokunuşla açıklanan akıl karışıklığını beden hareketi koşulu olmadan daha genel verir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da akıl bozukluğunu görünmez bir varlığın etkisiyle açıklayan geleneksel anlayışta buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal belirli bir kaynak ilişkilendirmesi ve istemsiz baş-gövde hareketi gerektirir; komşu dal daha genel bir doğaüstü dokunuş açıklamasıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; doğaüstü etkiye bağlanan akıl bozukluğu çekirdeğini en doğrudan paylaşan komşu yayımlandı.

word_morpheme_spans.note: Accepted bridge links preserve independent analysis identities. Several analysis entries may share canonical morphemes. Read their distinct semantic claims; shared morphology alone is not duplication. Legacy aligned_qac_word_ref values are source observations, not QAC joins. Excluded source entries remain available with their explicit qualification.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: Legacy analysis and QAC numbers are separate source namespaces. Use accepted word_morpheme_spans for actual many-to-many joins. The legacy numbering observation is preserved, not used for alignment.

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.
